items.title: Wendell Brunious interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000 [interview 2 of 2]

ctx.x: And this guy, his name was Vladimir Vasiliev, and he had gone to Berklee in Boston and studied with Margaret Chaloff. Come to find out Lew Soloff was his first trumpet player when Lew was about 19 or 20 years old. And I was telling Lew this story, and he was like, “My God man, I had forgotten about Vladimir.” But that kind of — then I started making a little money and then it was like hey, I could actually make a living doing this. So Vladimir had a great Latin band, which he had like Al McKibbon and Don Alias…

called Wallace and said, “Hey, who’s that boy that you had down there?” So Bill Titone called me and Wallace says, “Look, whatever kind of money they offer you, take it. That’s an experience that you can’t buy. Just take the job man.” He says, “Just take the job. In the future you’re not even going to think about it but it will help you so much.” So I did about five months of staying in the YMCA in New York.
